title: Reasoning about Continuous-Variable Quantum Systems
authors: Tianshi Yu, Gilles Barthe, Minbo Gao, Mingsheng Ying, Li Zhou
abstract: Continuous-variable quantum computing (CVQC) is a computing paradigm in which measurements yield values over a continuous domain. CVQC is both a convenient omputational framework for modeling physical quantum systems, and a good abstraction for hardware platforms based on quantum optics. Yet, the semantic foundations of CVQC remain underdeveloped. To address this gap, we develop a formal semantics for a core CV quantum programming language, and sound verification methods for program correctness.   A main contribution of this work is to isolate a well-behaved quantitative predicate domain that achieves sufficient expressiveness to accommodate unbounded values as they arise in the infinite-dimensional, continuous setting. Specifically, we choose closed positive quadratic forms as semantic predicates, representing finite expectations, domains of finiteness, and infinite penalties in one ordered object. We validate our choice by establishing that our semantic predicates satisfy desirable closure properties including the definition of weakest preconditions.   We validate our design with two case studies, including an example based on the celebrated GKP error-correcting code, for which we establish a second moment bound.
summary: This paper develops a formal semantics for Continuous-Variable Quantum Computing (CVQC) by defining a specialized logic that can handle unbounded values. It introduces closed positive quadratic forms as semantic predicates to reason about expected costs and error bounds. This framework is validated using the GKP code, providing tools for verifying quantum algorithms in continuous settings.
main_problem: The work aims to develop a formal semantics and sound verification methods for Continuous-Variable Quantum Computing (CVQC) programs.
main_result: A formal semantics is established using closed positive quadratic forms as semantic predicates, allowing the rigorous reasoning about unbounded values inherent in continuous quantum systems.
method: The authors extend Hoare logic with a cost-parameterized weakest precondition ($	ext{wp}_c$) and define the predicate domain using closed positive quadratic forms to handle infinite-dimensional expectations.
model_or_system: The focus is on CVQC paradigms, particularly those based on quantum optics, and includes validation via the Gottesman–Kitaev–Preskill (GKP) error-correcting code protocol.
key_observables: Expected cost, hard constraints, error bounds (e.g., second moment bound for GKP), and position variance ($\hat{q}^2$).
important_parameters: The structure of the semantic predicates must accommodate unbounded values arising from continuous measurements.
main_assumptions: Existing weakest-precondition calculus often uses bounded predicates, which is insufficient for the unbounded expectations required in CVQC.
paper_structure: The paper develops a formal semantics for a quantum while-language over separable Hilbert spaces, defines the predicate domain using closed positive quadratic forms, and validates this with case studies including GKP error correction.
why_interesting: This work provides the necessary mathematical rigor to analyze complex continuous measurements and feedback loops common in quantum optics experiments, bridging theoretical computation models with physical constraints.
